title: Evening Rehras, lived
hookLine: the evening prayer as work ends
tomorrow: what did Bhai Lalo's plain bread have that a rich man's feast didn't?

cards: Here's something odd in the Sikh day. As work ends and the light goes, Sikhs say Rehras, the evening prayer.

And Rehras opens with a question you may have already said that morning, inside Japji: what is that door, and what is that house, where you sit and take care of all? The same question, at both ends of the day.

teach.b: The hymn is called So Dar, that door, and it appears more than once in the Granth: in Japji, in Rehras, and again in Raag Asa. The puzzle solves itself when you keep reading.
Guru Nanak doesn't answer with a map to the door. He describes who's singing there. In paraphrase: countless instruments sound, countless players play.
Air, water and fire sing at your door. The seekers sing, the faithful, the generous, the warriors.
All of creation is a choir at that door.
In the morning, the question goes out with you, unanswered, into a day of errands and orders.
In the evening it comes back, and now there's a whole day to hold up against it: the bus, the shift, the friend who needed you, the sky going orange. You notice who was singing all along.
That's why it's a prayer for dusk. The day doesn't get solved.
It gets put down, at that door, where everything else has been singing the whole time.

how: Sikhs recite Rehras Sahib in the evening, around sunset as the working day ends, at home or in the gurdwara; it opens with So Dar and continues with further hymns and banis.

o: the hymn sung at a Sikh wedding as the couple walks
a prayer of asking for help with tomorrow's work
the prayer at dusk, opening with 'what is that door?'

games.q: your cousin says Rehras opening with So Dar is 'just Japji again, so why bother?' what's the puzzle's best answer?
o: the same question lands differently at dusk: a whole day comes back to that door.
it's a copying slip in the Granth that nobody has ever gone back to fix.
the evening prayer needed to be longer, so verses were added to pad it.
games.why: in the morning the question goes out with you; at dusk you hold a whole day up to it and notice who was singing all along.

practice: Look out a window, or at one light in the room, and watch it as it is right now. Name one thing from today, and set it down, the way you'd set a bag down at a door. Then let the sit hold the quiet after.

wordCard.voice: Evening Rehras. The prayer at dusk as work ends, opening with So Dar: what is that door?

orig.note: Gurmukhi: so dar, that door: the hymn that opens Rehras.

carryVoice: Carry this: the day put down, not solved, just set down at the door. Good night's coming.
